headline: Supreme Infrastructure gets NCLT deadline extension to October 31 for ₹2,200 crore debt settlement
hook: Extension buys time for major lenders
summary: The National Company Law Tribunal in Mumbai has extended the payment deadline to October 31 for Supreme Infrastructure to settle its ₹2,200 crore debt. State Bank of India, Punjab National Bank, and Union Bank of India have agreed on a framework to complete these settlement obligations. This extension provides the distressed infrastructure firm crucial breathing room to finalize repayment terms with its primary institutional creditors. Retail investors holding exposure to these public sector banks should note the ongoing resolution of legacy stressed assets.
whats_next: October 31 payment deadline for settlement completion
why_it_matters: Debt resolution progress clears legacy stress for lender banks.
winners_losers: Supreme Infrastructure gains / lenders clear bad loans

headline: PNB suspends five employees over a Rs 22-crore bank fraud in Greater Noida
hook: Jewar land compensation funds vanish in fraud
summary: An alleged Rs 22-crore bank fraud at Punjab National Bank's Greater Noida branch has blocked account access for customers, including those holding Jewar airport land compensation and fixed deposits. Preliminary findings show funds were illicitly transferred to accounts in Jharkhand. PNB has suspended five employees, transferred remaining staff, and begun refunding affected customers while approaching the CBI. Police have received 37 complaints as the investigation continues. Indian retail depositors face growing concerns regarding internal bank operational security and account safety.
why_it_matters: Bank branch fraud risks depositor savings and highlights internal control gaps.

headline: Punjab National Bank revises credit card ATM withdrawal, late payment, and utility fees effective November 1
hook: New fee schedule hits cardholders next month
summary: Punjab National Bank has announced a revised fee structure for its Visa and RuPay credit card users, taking effect from November 1, 2026. The changes cover ATM cash withdrawal fees, late payment penalties, utility bill transaction charges, and reward point redemption costs. These updates will directly impact everyday card operations and transaction costs for retail customers. Indian retail holders of PNB credit cards will face altered out-of-pocket expenses for routine banking and bill payments.
why_it_matters: Higher transaction and penalty fees increase everyday costs for PNB cardholders.

headline: PNB updates credit card fee structure starting November
hook: Higher costs for PNB credit card users
summary: Punjab National Bank is revising its credit card fee and charge structure effective November 1. The changes include adjustments to late payment fees, finance charges, and other service-related costs. These updates apply to all existing credit card holders of the bank. Retail customers should review their specific card terms to understand how these revised charges impact their monthly billing.
why_it_matters: Higher credit card fees increase your monthly debt servicing costs.
winners_losers: PNB gains / Credit card users hurt

headline: PNB suspends 12 employees over missing customer funds
hook: Unauthorised withdrawals hit PNB customer accounts
summary: Punjab National Bank has suspended 12 employees following the disappearance of ₹11.24 crore from customer accounts at its Greater Noida branch. The bank is currently investigating the unauthorised withdrawals alongside ongoing customer claims. This incident highlights potential internal control lapses at the branch level. Retail investors should note the operational risk and potential reputational impact on the bank's governance.
why_it_matters: Operational lapses may trigger regulatory scrutiny and impact bank stock sentiment.

headline: Punjab National Bank promises to settle genuine claims after branch fraud
hook: PNB addresses Greater Noida branch fraud
summary: Punjab National Bank has assured customers that all legitimate claims will be settled following a fraud incident at its Greater Noida branch. The bank is currently addressing the fallout from the unauthorized activities reported at the location. This development aims to maintain customer trust and prevent panic among depositors. Retail investors should note the bank's proactive stance in mitigating potential reputational and financial risks.
why_it_matters: Depositor confidence remains intact despite localized branch fraud issues.

headline: Punjab National Bank settles three claims worth Rs 43 lakh related to a Greater Noida branch fraud case.
hook: Three claims settled in PNB fraud case
summary: State-owned lender Punjab National Bank has settled three claims totaling Rs 43 lakh in connection with a fraud case reported at its Greater Noida branch. The resolution is part of ongoing recovery and settlement efforts by the public sector bank regarding the specific branch incident. Indian retail investors holding PNB shares can track asset quality and provisioning updates from such legacy fraud cases. The settlement amounts are relatively small for a large-cap PSU lender.
why_it_matters: Minimal financial impact on large-cap bank earnings.

headline: PNB outlines recovery process for Rs 35 crore fraud victims
hook: Legal recourse for PNB fraud victims
summary: Punjab National Bank has detailed the rights of account holders affected by a Rs 35 crore fraud case. The bank has outlined specific steps for customers to seek full recovery of their lost funds. This guidance follows internal investigations into the unauthorized transactions. Retail investors should note the bank's liability protocols and the formal grievance redressal mechanisms available.
why_it_matters: Clarifies recovery rights for bank customers impacted by fraud.

headline: PNB settles Rs 43 lakh in claims over Greater Noida branch fraud
hook: Unauthorised transfers hit savings and fixed deposits
summary: Punjab National Bank has settled three claims totaling Rs 43 lakh following complaints of alleged unauthorised transfers from savings accounts and fixed deposits at its Greater Noida branch. By Wednesday, 25 customers had lodged complaints with the bank regarding the suspicious activity. The bank is addressing the grievances as complaints continue to mount from affected account holders. Retail investors should note operational risk developments at public sector banks.
why_it_matters: Branch-level fraud risks weigh on public bank operational trust

headline: RBI imposes Rs 1.56 crore penalty on Punjab National Bank
summary: The Reserve Bank of India has levied a financial penalty of Rs 1.56 crore on Punjab National Bank for non-compliance with certain operational guidelines. The regulatory action follows statutory inspections regarding the bank's adherence to directives. PNB shareholders face compliance risks and potential negative sentiment from the penalty. Retail investors should track regulatory compliance costs affecting the bank's bottom line.
why_it_matters: Compliance penalties weigh on PNB's near-term profitability

headline: PNB suspends 12 employees following Rs 10 crore fraud
hook: Internal fraud detected at PNB branch
summary: Punjab National Bank has suspended 12 employees after discovering unauthorized fund transfers executed using a branch manager's password. The bank identified a female employee who allegedly colluded with external parties to facilitate the transactions. PNB clarified that the total loss is under Rs 10 crore, refuting higher figures circulating on social media. The bank has filed a formal case with the CBI to investigate the matter.
why_it_matters: Minor operational lapses highlight internal control risks for bank shareholders.

headline: Punjab National Bank reports 13 percent rise in Q2 net profit
summary: Punjab National Bank reported a standalone net profit of Rs 10,785.52 crore for the second quarter. This marks a 13 percent increase compared to the Rs 6,578.73 crore profit recorded in the same period last year. The bank's shares rose 2 percent following the announcement of these financial results.
why_it_matters: Stronger earnings may support PNB stock price momentum

headline: Farmers' fixed deposits vanish from a Punjab National Bank branch
hook: Millions missing from a rural Punjab branch
summary: Fixed deposits belonging to farmers at a Punjab National Bank branch have mysteriously vanished from their accounts without their authorization. The incident has raised serious questions about operational security and internal controls at public sector banks. Account holders face sudden financial distress and loss of hard-earned savings. Indian retail investors should monitor governance and audit standards across PSU banks.
whats_next: Bank audit and police investigation findings
why_it_matters: PSU bank governance risks can hurt depositor trust and valuations

headline: PNB suspends branch manager and four others after Greater Noida customers report Rs 35 crore missing from accounts
hook: Thirty five crore rupees missing at branch
summary: Punjab National Bank has suspended its branch manager and four other employees in Greater Noida following customer complaints alleging that Rs 35 crore has gone missing from their accounts. The bank has initiated an internal inquiry to investigate the missing funds and account discrepancies. Customers discovered the missing balances while updating their passbooks, leading to protests at the branch. For Indian retail investors, such operational and fraud risks at public sector banks can trigger temporary negative sentiment and heightened regulatory scrutiny.
whats_next: Internal probe findings and police investigation updates
why_it_matters: Branch-level fraud incidents can weigh on investor sentiment for the bank.

headline: PNB suspends five employees after customer fixed deposits worth crores disappear
hook: Crores vanish from customer fixed deposits
summary: Punjab National Bank has suspended five employees following the mysterious disappearance of fixed deposits worth crores from several customer accounts. The incident has triggered customer protests alongside parallel bank and police investigations. Indian retail investors holding shares in the state-owned lender face potential reputational damage and governance concerns. Account security issues at major public sector banks can erode depositor trust and weigh on near-term stock sentiment.
